Short answers about using 1NEON. Signed in? Tap ? at the top right of any page for help with that page.

Getting started

What is 1NEON?

The portal where you and I run your projects together. Each project keeps what you need, the work, the results, and the handover in one place. Watch it.

Can I try it first?

Yes, three ways, and none needs an account. The guided walkthrough plays a fictional project on the real portal in about two minutes, with controls to pause, pick a chapter, or exit; the full story takes about six. The interactive demo is a working copy with made-up clients where you pick who to be and try anything; your changes stay in your browser until you choose Start over. The sample project is one made-up project to read at your own pace, from request to handover. With a couple of minutes to spare, start with the walkthrough. Short walkthroughs show a single thing: joining from an invitation, adding a passkey, adding an authenticator app, and texts and text codes.

How do I get in?

You need an invite. Open the link in your invite email and enter your email address. Sign in with a code sent to your email, or with a passkey. No password needed. Watch it.

I didn't get the sign-in code.

Check your spam or promotions folder, then wait a minute and choose Send a new code. Codes work for a few minutes, in the browser where you asked for them. Watch it.

Is there a tour?

Yes. It's offered the first time you sign in. Skip it or ask to be reminded next time, and replay it anytime from ? at the top right or from your profile. Watch it.

Projects and the four layers

What are Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize?

The four layers every project moves through, N E O N. Needs is what you want and the options to get there. Execute is the work. Observe checks the results against the goals. Normalize makes the change last: handover, training, and care. Watch it.

What should I do first on a project?

Look at Next step at the top of the project. It says what has to happen now and who it's waiting on, and it changes as soon as that's done: approve an option or send a file and it moves on to the next thing. When nothing is waiting on anyone, it names the stage's goal and offers Move to the next stage. Watch it.

What do Not started, On track, At risk, and Off track mean?

They're the project's health. A new project is Not started, and it turns On track by itself once it moves past its first stage or any of its work is in progress or done. After that, the team sets it on the project's overview, or with a status update. Items have their own status in their panel: To do, In progress, Blocked, or Done. Watch it.

What if we rename, reorder, or hide stages?

Projects follow along. Their steps, the board, and Next step use the new names and order. A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it. Decide keeps asking for an approved option, and Closed still ends a project, under any name or position.

How do I tell you what I need?

Open the project's Needs tab and tap Add request. Finish a sentence with a few taps: what you'd like to do (choose any, or tap + to add your own), what it's for, what happens currently, how often it happens, and when it's due, including a date or a date range. Tap Define another need to add more. Each need becomes its own request, and only the first choice is required. Watch it.

Do I have to write a lot?

No. Each section says what belongs there, shows an example, and offers suggestions you can add with one tap. Discovery questions take a short answer right where they're asked, and a real example helps most. Watch it.

How do I know when something changes?

The bell at the top glows softly when something new happens, like a file upload, a decision, or a project moving stage. Tap it to see what changed and who did it, then tap one to open it. Important changes also email you; choose which in your profile under Notifications. Watch it.

How do I comment or change an item?

Tap the item's title. A panel opens with its status, owner, due date, and details, and a place to comment. Everyone in your organization sees the comments. Options and measures open the same way, with their cost and scores, or unit and target, there too. Watch it.

How do I check something off?

Tick the box beside it. Every item that can be finished has one, and the counts on each tab and section show how many are done. A choice between options counts as one, done once an option is approved, and a measure counts as done when it reaches its target. Status updates and decisions are records, so they don't count. Files you upload aren't counted either; a File needed is, and it's checked off when you send the file. Watch it.

How do I delete something?

Use the trash button on the item, or Delete in its panel. Either one asks first. Approved options and decisions can't be deleted, since they're the record of what was agreed. Options themselves come from neon1. Files have their own Delete for the person who uploaded them and admins.

What does the onion next to a project mean?

It shows progress. Needs is the center ring and Normalize is the outside one. Each ring fills as that layer's work gets done.

What does the board show?

Every project as a card, in the stage it's in. Columns run left to right from the first call to care after handover. Drag a card to move it, or use its Move to menu on a phone. A closed project moves back the same way, or use Reopen on its page. Watch it.

What does the timeline show?

Under Projects, Timeline draws each project from the day it started to its target date, colored by its layer. The dashed line is today, the diamond is the target, the lighter part is time still ahead, and red stripes are time past the target. Each row also says its stage and how many days are left. Watch it.

How do I start a project?

Choose New project, answer a few short questions, and the project starts with a checklist that fits. You can change everything later. Watch it.

What is Coming up on Home?

This week and the next two as a strip of days. Each mark is something dated: a task's due date, a milestone, or a project's target. Below it, everything dated in the next six weeks is listed by Overdue, This week, Next week, and Later. Watch it.

What is Insights?

Charts made from your organization's own data: open and overdue work, how often things finish on time, days to a decision, work finished per week, where projects sit across the four layers, and how healthy they are. Watch it.

Decisions and approvals

How do I approve an option?

Open the project's Needs layer, compare the options, and choose Approve this option. You can add conditions, such as "only after 6pm". The approval is recorded with your name, the time, and a copy of the option's terms (title, description, cost, and timeline) exactly as you saw them. Options come from neon1; to ask for a change, comment on the option. Watch it.

Who can approve?

The person named as the project's decision maker. If nobody is named, an admin of your organization can. Only an admin of your organization can name or change the decision maker, under People on the project's overview, after confirming it's them; editors can change everyone else on the project. Each change is recorded with the old and new decision maker, and neon1 can't be named, since it proposes the options. (In neon1's own organization, where neon1 is the client, it can.) Watch it.

Can an approval be changed?

Not edited. Once approved, neither the decision nor the option it came from can be edited or removed. To change course, a new option is proposed and approved. The earlier decision stays on record, marked as replaced, so the history stays clear.

What do Cost, Quality, and Effort mean?

They're neon1's assessment of each option, from 1 to 5, where more filled dots is always better. Cost is the total cost. Quality is how fully it meets the requirements you agreed. Effort is your team's effort to adopt and run it. Each option also lists one-time and recurring charges apart, with a first-year total when it has both; the written price on the option is what you'd agree to. Figures in the demo and the walkthrough are illustrative. Watch it.

Files

How do I send a file?

Use Upload next to a file I asked for, or go to Files and upload it there. Pick the project it belongs to. Tap a file's name to open it: PDFs, pictures, and text open in a new tab, and anything else downloads. Watch it.

Are files safe?

Every file is checked for viruses before anyone can download it, and stays private to your organization. Please don't upload passwords or keys.

What can I upload?

Any kind of file, up to 100 MB each. Please don't upload passwords, keys, or other secrets, malware, or regulated data such as health or payment card details unless we have a written agreement that covers it.

People and access

What can viewers, editors, and admins do?

Viewers read and comment. Editors also add and change work. Admins also invite people, change their access, and change settings. neon1's own access is set by neon1, so it shows on People without a way to change it. Watch it.

How do I invite someone?

Admins go to People and choose Invite people. The person gets an email with a link. People shows whether each invitation email went out; if one didn't, or it got lost, choose Resend. Watch it.

Can 1NEON text me?

Once texts are switched on, yes. Add your mobile number on your profile, agree to texts, save, then type the code 1NEON texts you. Texts only say that something new is waiting, with a link; they never name your organization, projects, or files. Reply STOP to any text to turn them off. Watch it.

Why does it ask me to confirm it's me?

Admin actions (inviting people, changing access or settings, and deleting a project or someone else's comment or file) also need a recent confirmation with a passkey, an authenticator app, or a text-message code. That way a stolen email account isn't enough to make changes. On your profile, under Two-step verification, add any of the three, then confirm with it when asked. A second one is a backup if you lose the first. Once confirmed, you won't be asked again for 12 hours in that sign-in. Watch it.

Can I use an authenticator app?

Yes. On your profile, choose Set up next to Authenticator app, scan the code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, or similar, and type the 6-digit code it shows. Watch it.

What's a passkey?

A sign-in that uses your face, fingerprint, or device PIN instead of a code. It's faster, and it's phishing-resistant: it only works on the real 1NEON site, so a look-alike page can't use it. Add one on your profile under Two-step verification; next time you sign in, 1NEON offers it first. Watch it.

Your account

How do I change my name or the look?

Open your profile from the menu. You can change your name, title, theme, menu, and notifications there, then choose Save. The menu button (top left, and Menu at the bottom on phones) opens the full menu; choose Mini to also keep a slim menu of icons on the left. Two-step verification and signing out work right away. Watch it.

How do I sign out?

Open your profile and choose Sign out.

I lost my phone or my authenticator app.

You can still sign in with a code sent to your email. The second step is only needed for admin actions, such as inviting people or changing settings. If you set up another method, confirm it's you with that one, then remove the lost one under Two-step verification on your profile and add a new one. If you've lost every method, email hello@neon1.tech from your account's address. The portal has no self-service reset for a lost second step.

My email address changed.

Your email address is how 1NEON knows you, and it can't be changed on your profile. Ask an admin of your organization to invite your new address and deactivate the old one, or email hello@neon1.tech. Work done under the old address stays in the record under that name.

Who do I ask for access?

An admin of your organization. Admins invite people and change their access. If you don't know who that is, or neon1's own access needs to change, email hello@neon1.tech.

Support, billing, and your data

What does approving an option commit us to?

An approval records that your organization agreed to that option as shown: its scope, cost, and timeline, plus any conditions you added. Both sides can rely on that record. It works alongside your signed agreement with neon1, which governs the paid work.

Where are invoices and payments?

Not in 1NEON. Invoices and payment happen outside the portal, as your signed agreement sets out.

Something urgent is wrong. Who do I tell?

Email hello@neon1.tech with what happened and when. neon1 works planned hours, with no 24/7 or emergency response, so for something that can't wait, such as a fraud on your bank account or an outage your business can't run without, contact the provider responsible first. Report a security problem in the portal itself to security@neon1.tech.

Can we get a copy of our data?

Yes. There's no export button, so ask at hello@neon1.tech and I'll send your organization's data in a common format.

What happens to our data when the work ends?

It's kept as the record of our work together, so either of us can refer back to it, unless your organization asks me to delete it. Your organization can stop using 1NEON at any time and ask for an export first. The privacy policy has the details, including how long backups and audit records last.

Who can I contact?

Email hello@neon1.tech.
